Maya (Platform): Heads up — product wants header-driven model selection for the API. they want: x-model-alias, optional version pin, and a safety fallback. can we map that to routing rules without exploding the policy matrix?
Tom (API): short answer: yes. we already match on headers for routing. question: should alias->model be resolved at gateway or in the routing service?
Anil (Runtime): prefer resolving at gateway for latency, but runtime needs to check compatibility constraints (tokenizer, kv-cache layout) before loading model. otherwise we get runtime errors.
Jess (Console): if gateway resolves alias, console UX needs to surface what alias maps to and allow pinning via UI (canary slider + rollout %). also need to show effective config per route.
Maya (Platform): propose flow: 1) gateway checks header x-model-alias -> maps to alias entry; 2) alias entry includes optional pinned_version and compatibility tags; 3) gateway enforces pin if present, otherwise resolves to alias.default; 4) if compatibility mismatch -> fallback to alias.fallback_model.
Tom (API): example config idea (pseudo):
```yaml
routes:
  - path: /v1/chat/completions
    match_headers:
      x-model-alias: required
    model_selection:
      alias_key: user-facing-alias
      allow_pin: true
      enforce_compatibility: true
      fallback: small-compat-v1
```
Anil (Runtime): +1 but add explicit `compatibility_tags` like `["kv-v1","tokenizer-bpe"]`. gateway should check that target model has superset of tags required by route.
Sara (SRE): how do quotas apply? if alias maps to multiple backends (hosted/dedicated/private) we need to ensure quota billing is correct. do we meter by actual model instance or by alias resolution?
Maya (Platform): we should meter by the resolved model instance (the actual runtime serving the request). that maps to billing/tenant. alias is just a logical name. but console should show aggregated usage per alias and per model.
Jess (Console): UI items: alias detail page with history of resolutions (time series), current pinned version, active rollouts, and a toggle to force pin for a route. also show compatibility warnings before pinning.
Tom (API): edge case: client sends `x-model-version` header along with alias. should api respect that even if alias.locked? suggestion: default: header overrides pin only if caller has `override:model-pin` entitlement. otherwise ignore.
Maya (Platform): agree on entitlement gate. we should also emit telemetry events: `alias_resolved`, `alias_fallback`, `pin_override_attempt` with fields: route, alias, resolved_model, reason.
Anil (Runtime): telemetry should include `compat_check_passed` boolean and `compat_mismatch_reason` string if failed. runtime will reject if mismatch and gateway fallback not configured.
Sara (SRE): deploy plan? small rollout: enable header-match routing behind feature flag, run canary for 10% traffic for 24h. have an automated rollback if errors spike > 3x baseline.
Maya (Platform): action items: @Tom add gateway resolution impl PR with config proto; @Anil add compat tags enforcement and telemetry hooks; @Jess wire up alias UI and aggregated metrics; @Sara add canary and alert runbook. I'll create tickets.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: gateway/feature/alias-routing -> staging. queued by Maya.
Tom (API): quick note — implement config so route-level `enforce_compatibility` defaults to true. we can add an escape flag but should be explicit.
Jess (Console): will mock UX in figma today, pinging for feedback.
Maya (Platform): thanks all. if anyone sees major gaps call out now. otherwise i'll spin the tickets and link to the PRs. :thumbsup:
